title: Prime-to-p root limit and compatible primitive families
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $p\in\mathbf N$. Put $D_p=\{m\in\mathbf N:0<m,\ \gcd(m,p)=1\}$. For $m\in D_p$, let $\mu_m(k)=\{z\in k^\times:z^m=1\}$. Define $G(k,p)$ to be the subgroup of $\prod_{m\in D_p}k^\times$ consisting of the families $x$ such that $x_m\in\mu_m(k)$ and $x_n^{n/m}=x_m$ whenever $m\mid n$. Equip $G(k,p)$ with the coarsest topology for which every coordinate map into the discrete group $k^\times$ is continuous, equivalently the inverse-limit topology of the discrete root groups. A family $\zeta:D_p\to k^\times$ is a compatible primitive family if every $\zeta_m$ has multiplicative order exactly $m$, $\zeta_1=1$, and $\zeta_n^{n/m}=\zeta_m$ whenever $m\mid n$.
